output.title: Spot proof-of-concept debt before you call the pilot done
output.body:
This is for the owner of a 1–10 person business. If you have tried ChatGPT but not wired it into a real workflow, proof-of-concept debt is the awkward bit you leave behind in a pilot: a missing doc, an untested edge case, a manual workaround, or a bug you hope can wait.

The mistake is not that debt exists. The mistake is treating every deferred item as if it belongs in the same bucket.

Use one simple decision rule at pilot close: is this still a one-off proof, or has it become something you now need to extend into production? If it is still a proof, keep the deferred items in a separate post-pilot list. If it has become a production candidate, pause expansion until the deferred list is reviewed and priced as real scope.

The practical next step is to write three columns before you sign off: what was deferred, why it was deferred, and whether each item is essential before rollout or genuinely post-launch. Review that page with the owner before anyone calls the pilot complete. Keep it as a working record, not a legal warranty. That small sheet of paper is often the difference between a clean decision and a surprise hidden in the margin.
